review_scope: Concept/model sheet only; no sprite, moveset, animation, SMS conversion or ROM approval.

source_evidence.role: owner-approved identity, face, palette, proportions and style reference

references.role: project character identity and source-game inventory
weapon reference boundary and source terminology discrepancy

observed_defects: The source-game item terminology differs between the GDD and combat proposal/community guide. The new arsenal panel is explicitly reference-only until the project resolves that discrepancy.
The action arm and cane grip read more clearly in the producer inspection, but shoulder/elbow/wrist continuity still needs an independent reviewer.
revision_notes: Front/profile/back costume cues were aligned to a late-19th-century London investigator while preserving face, lean body, palette, 7.5H scale and the profile pose.
The signature action now pairs a visibly connected boomerang release with a blunt walking cane held in the other hand; no rapier/sword thrust is shown.
An adjacent, labeled equipment panel separates concept identity objects from the source-game arsenal references.

document_and_layout.note: Five model views, shared ruler/baseline, style cards and an adjacent two-group equipment panel are visible; no main figure or equipment is visibly cropped.

style_reference_application.note: Producer inspection sees the established 1990s fighting-game cel concept language and cream technical-sheet treatment; independent comparison remains required before promotion.

lineart_and_contours.note: Contours appear clean and the figure/equipment silhouettes remain separated at sheet scale; independent review remains required.

morphology_and_biotype.note: Tall, lean adult ectomorph proportions and the established 7.5H guide are retained; no chibi or bulky redesign is visible.

shading_and_palette.note: Blue/cyan/teal, white, gray, burgundy and brass/brown remain the dominant palette; violet remains confined to the occult boomerang effect.

relative_scale_and_baseline.note: The orthographic figures share a common baseline and the 7.5H ruler remains visible.

neutral_background.note: The page uses a clean pale-cream background without scenery or texture.

face_and_identity_continuity.note: Gray hair, brass spectacles, mature intelligent face and fully human identity remain aligned to the approved v2 reference.

costume_and_materials.note: The long frock-coat tails/lapels, waistcoat, high collar, burgundy cravat and watch-chain cue read more clearly as late-Victorian London attire across the turnaround.

equipment_and_weapon_continuity.note: The cane is distinct from the rapier, but independent review found the source-game inventory terminology differs across project documents; list remains reference-only and unresolved.

cross_view_consistency.note: Front, profile and back keep the same coat family, palette, body scale and character identity; the profile pose remains consistent with the reference.

legibility_and_crop_integrity.note: The title, candidate status, equipment labels and technical cards are visible at the saved resolution; no object touches a page edge.

human_traits_and_unapproved_details.note: The figure remains fully human; no fangs, wings, vampiric transformation or unrequested costume props are visible.

artist_reference_and_scope.note: The CPS2-Alpha-Cel reference role is carried forward from the approved v2 lineage; it is a contextual style reference, not a sole-authorship claim.

distinctive_style_signature.note: Expressive fighting-game face planes, clean graphic silhouette and high-energy action staging are retained.

pose_anatomy_and_joint_continuity.note: Independent review found the cane hand and wrist visible but the sleeve/elbow partially disappear into the torso, leaving an arm-emergence ambiguity at sheet scale.

visual_cohesion_and_distinction.note: Identity/style cohesion is positive, but independent reviewer requested clearer steel-boomerang silhouette against violet motion curves.
